items.title: 15.5.2 Peripheral Nervous System - Cranial & Spinal Nerves

source_refs.note: Topic 15.5.2 with the table of cranial nerves (PDF 40-42); Figure 15.15 is redrawn as an original diagram beside the table, and Figure 15.16 is carried by the original diagram.

blocks.text: The peripheral nervous system consists of nerves, cable-like collections of axons, and ganglia, clusters of cell bodies outside the CNS. Nerves from the brain are cranial nerves; nerves from the spinal cord are spinal nerves.

There are 12 pairs of cranial nerves. The first two pairs (olfactory and optic) arise from the cerebrum and the other ten from the brainstem. Some are sensory, some motor and some mixed (carrying axons of both sensory and motor neurons).

blocks.caption: The twelve pairs of cranial nerves

sensation in the face; chewing muscles

taste at the back of the tongue; swallowing muscles

blocks.alt: The underside of the brain (cerebrum, pons, medulla, cerebellum, spinal cord) with twelve pairs of cranial nerves in order from front to back: I olfactory and II optic (sensory) from the cerebrum; from the brainstem III oculomotor, IV trochlear and VI abducens (motor), V trigeminal and VII facial (mixed), VIII vestibulocochlear (sensory), IX glossopharyngeal and X vagus (mixed), XI accessory and XII hypoglossal (motor). Sensory blue, motor red, mixed purple.
blocks.caption: Twelve pairs of cranial nerves seen from below the brain (original diagram after Figure 15.15).
blocks.long_description: Read with the table: the colour of each nerve shows whether it is sensory, motor or mixed. The first two pairs arise from the cerebrum and the other ten from the brainstem; the vagus (X) is the only one that reaches the organs of the chest and abdomen.

blocks.text: There are 31 pairs of spinal nerves, all mixed, carrying sensory and motor information between the spinal cord and the rest of the body. Each leaves the cord by two short roots: the dorsal root carries the axons and dendrites of sensory neurons, whose cell bodies lie together in the dorsal root ganglion outside the cord, and the ventral root carries the axons of motor neurons, whose cell bodies lie within the cord. The roots join just before the nerve leaves the vertebral column.

blocks.alt: Left: the meninges as layers from the outside in: bone, the thick dura mater, the thin arachnoid, a space with cerebrospinal fluid, the delicate pia mater, then the brain or spinal cord. Right: the spinal cord in cross-section, an oval of white matter round an H-shaped core of grey matter with a central canal; on each side a dorsal root with a ganglion and a ventral root join into a spinal nerve. A note lists the 31 pairs of spinal nerves.
blocks.caption: Spinal nerves and their roots (original diagram after Figure 15.16).
blocks.long_description: Three meninges cover the brain and spinal cord: the thick outer dura mater with larger vessels, the thin arachnoid that separates the cerebrospinal fluid below it from the blood in the dura, and the delicate pia mater on the surface, whose capillaries nourish the tissue. In the spinal cord the arrangement is the reverse of the brain: grey matter (cell bodies of inter-neurons and motor neurons) forms the inner H, white matter (myelinated axons) the outer zone, round a central canal continuous with the fourth ventricle. Each spinal nerve joins a dorsal root (sensory, with its cell bodies in the dorsal root ganglion) and a ventral root (motor). There are 31 pairs: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and 1 coccygeal.
